A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAG forecasting work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting results, component ablations, parameter sensitivity studies, lookback experiments and prediction visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and reports additional comparator results and full benchmark results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The temporal and channel modules, parameter transfer, gating, prediction fusion, losses and inference procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 also retains the same baseline adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: The dataset roster is unchanged: v2 Appendix A.1 already states that the eight common benchmarks were evaluated. v3 Tables 7–8 first report their results with and without future covariates, but v2 does not clearly specify those experiments' input conditions. Whether scenario coverage expanded or was merely documented remains uncertain.

E2.justification: GCGNet replaces DLinear in the matched 12-dataset comparisons, while the other comparators remain. xPatch, listed without reported scores in v2, participates in v3 Table 8.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, training setup and lookback/horizon settings of matched experiments are unchanged. The newly printed horizons for previously described common-benchmark experiments disclose settings without establishing a revision to an earlier protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablation results are identical in v2 Table 3 and v3 Table 4. Parameter sensitivity and lookback analyses move from Appendix B into Section 5.3; their plots, findings and the NP prediction visualizations are retained. The additional benchmark tables do not introduce a distinct diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. Table averages summarize forecasting horizons rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive four-horizon results for eight benchmarks in Tables 7–8, adds GCGNet scores and removes DLinear entries. Every retained score in the 12-dataset comparisons is unchanged, but comparator changes alter rankings: DAG's average MAE first-place count falls from 11 to 10. Section 5.2 still states 11.

T1.justification: The formal definitions and Equations 1–28 are unchanged, with no added proofs or derivations. Correcting the description of Equation 18 from temporal to channel correlation loss does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The Introduction replaces assertions about causal dependencies and dual causality with correlation-based framing, consistent with the new limitations discussion. The abstract, contribution list and principal forecasting claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.3 explicitly acknowledges the absence of causal modeling, limitations of dot-product gating and dependence on manually tuned loss and output weights. v2 lacks these specific qualifications; interpretations of the retained analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 7–8 newly disclose forecasting horizons of 96, 192, 336 and 720 for the eight common benchmarks already described in v2. Appendix A's software, hardware, optimizer, batch-size rules and fusion algorithm, together with the code/data access statement, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands citations in the Introduction and new Appendix B, covering additional forecasting research and numerous general vision/DNN works. Several earlier references disappear, including Sezer et al. and the xPatch reference, although xPatch now appears in Table 8. The central positioning against existing TSF-X methods remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the document: sensitivity and lookback sections move into the main text, Appendix B adds a citation-expanded repetition of related work, and experimental results are reorganized into Appendix C with limitations. The conclusion is shortened, and terminology, contact information and running headers are edited.

P2.justification: Dataset statistics and two analysis figures move into the main text, two full benchmark tables are added, and comparator columns change in matched tables. These substantially reorganize the presentation, although all original figure graphics are reused.

improvement.justification: The GCGNet comparisons and full results for previously described benchmarks make the empirical claims easier to assess, while Appendix C.3 appropriately qualifies the causal framing and design limitations. These gains outweigh limited presentation and consistency problems, including duplicated related work, the stale MAE win count, and insufficient explanation of future-covariate availability in Table 8.
